## Description

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind kep
/area dra

#### What this PR does / why we need it?

Defines device-count quota accounting for DRA `firstAvailable` requests in KEP-2941, behind the Alpha, default-off `KueueDRAIntegrationPrioritizedList` gate.

For each top-level `firstAvailable` request, Alpha requires every alternative to use a source-less mapping to the same logical resource and to ask for the same count. Kueue charges that count once. kube-scheduler selects exactly one alternative, and every alternative costs the same, so the charge equals whichever it selects. Independent requests remain additive, and PodSet scaling is unchanged. Alternatives with different counts are refused in Alpha; supporting them, with the reservation adjusted to the realized alternative after allocation, is a Beta criterion. The combinations Alpha rejects are listed in the KEP's support matrix.

The amendment covers the rule, what is rejected and why, how the charge meets the other scheduling features, the limitations, tests and graduation criteria; the Kubernetes API behind the feature, and what upstream says about quota, is summarized in the Appendix so the body states Kueue's rules only. The implementation is #14130.

Part of #13599. #13842 tracks the reservation-to-claim identity gap the KEP lists as a limitation.

#### Useful notes for your reviewer

The scope was narrowed in review from the maximum count among alternatives to alternatives that share a count; the maximum-count charge is now under Alternatives as the deferred path, and the accounting items raised in review are the Beta criteria for lifting the limit. The section text is @sohankunkerkar's rewrite of the earlier draft, taken as is with him as co-author. The fixed-template identity boundary (#13842) stays listed as a limitation, inherited from the `exactly` path. The KEP targets v0.20 for the Alpha, which #14130 implements. The branch is one commit.

_Disclosure: I used an AI coding assistant to help with the analysis and drafting of this update. I reviewed and verified the design, the code paths, and the KEP wording myself._

### Comment by [@thc1006](https://github.com/thc1006) — 2026-08-05T00:36:40Z

Pushed one more pass, mostly on the accounting contract.

The arithmetic paragraph was wrong in my own words. I had written that saturating sums mean nothing wraps negative, but `MapRequests.Add` uses plain `+`, so a DRA logical resource that shares a key with an ordinary Pod resource can still wrap. Saturation was also standing in for an upper bound it cannot carry, since clamping to `MaxInt64` reports less than the total it replaced. The contract is now exact-or-reject at each step that can produce an unrepresentable charge, and a saturated aggregate is not divided to recover a smaller request, which is what `PodSetResources` scaling does today for partial admission, `ReclaimablePods` and workload-slice replacement.

The conversion back to `int64` follows `resources.ResourceValue` rather than an unconditional `SafeValue`. That helper is milli-units for `cpu`, and nothing currently stops an administrator naming a logical resource `cpu`, where `8` would be read as 8 milliCPU.

MultiKueue said `firstAvailable` is out of scope and explained why, without saying what happens. It now says the admission check rejects before any remote Workload or Job exists, so the local reservation is released rather than an envelope being dispatched that the worker would not reproduce, and that a template that cannot be read yet stays retryable.

The ResourceClaimTemplate reuse gap is now called a known limitation with its tracking issue rather than a prerequisite, since the bound is already stated for a fixed claim spec, and the test plan covers the guarantees added here.

### Comment by [@thc1006](https://github.com/thc1006) — 2026-09-02T11:34:45Z

TL;DR: one more round, and two of the changes reverse earlier decisions rather than refine them. @sohankunkerkar `capacity` is charged now and I replied on your thread. @kannon92 the KEP is three commits, and I will squash before this merges.

**The design contract and the current branch were mixed together.** A paragraph described what the check in #14130 does today, in the present tense, while the graduation criteria said the full checker was required. A reader could not tell which of those was the Alpha bar. It reads as a MUST now: preprocessing carries the logical resource names the envelopes reached, and the shared request builder checks the fully merged value for each, including ordinary requests, overhead, transformation outputs, `Exactly` charges, the PodSet multiplication and the cross-PodSet aggregation. Where the prototype has got to lives in #14130.

**`excludeResourcePrefixes` no longer refuses a `firstAvailable` request.** The filter applies to the Pod's own requests, before transformations, and a name an explicit mapping synthesizes is not one of them, which is what the `Exactly` path has always done. Refusing the newer shape over the same pair of settings gave one administrator configuration two meanings depending on how a user wrote their claim, and put the refusal on an author who can change neither. Whether such an overlap should be refused belongs with configuration validation, across every mapping, and is worth its own issue.

The rest of the round:

- Classification is two stages. The first reads the API shape with no gate and no mapping, the second is the disposition. MultiKueue needs only the first, so a rollback cannot take its refusal with it.
- The DRA boundary returns a result, a verdict and an error rather than one `field.ErrorList`. A failed template read and an unknown allocation mode are both marked inadmissible today, and wrapping the first in `field.InternalError` does not make it retryable.
- `Info.Update` assigns `Obj` before it rebuilds, so an error path there would leave the new Workload beside the old totals. It has to commit in one step.
- There is no `ResourceClaimTemplate` watcher, so recovery after a template is deleted and recreated needs an index and a watch. The KEP no longer describes it as something that already happens.
- `IgnoreUndeclared` waives the quota decision, not the exact conversion, the non-negative operand or the range.
- Validating against the spec count is a utilization tradeoff, not something the first `TotalRequests` mechanically has to hold. I had the reason wrong last round.
- The global check before flavors are assigned is deliberately stricter than the accounting that follows, since the pending and unassigned representations carry no flavor dimension.
- The e2e forces the fallback with a fixture of one preferred and two fallback devices, rather than submitting a workload where a fallback is merely possible and passing whatever happens.

In #14130, the bounds check ran whether or not the gate was on, so an `Exactly`-only workload whose charge reaches the range was refused where it used to saturate. That is a change outside the gate, which is the one thing turning a gate off should rule out, so it is behind the gate now with a test either side of it.

`make verify` passes and the branch is rebased on main. Two Alpha policy calls are worth a second opinion, since both fail closed but neither is forced: charging `capacity` under a source-less mapping, and refusing on the spec count rather than letting partial admission rescue a request. Happy to take the narrower reading on either.

This comment was written in part with the assistance of generative AI. The code paths and the issue references above are ones I checked myself.

### Comment by [@thc1006](https://github.com/thc1006) — 2026-09-04T05:52:35Z

Rebased onto `e1460b6` and pushed. The KEP is about a thousand lines smaller than it was two rounds ago.

The last two rounds answered a long review pass on the queue and status state machine, and then took the answer back out. The design was right but it was not prioritized-list design. The condition a DRA verdict is written to, its reasons and triggers, the typed verdict model, the migration off the previous `Requeued` latch, the fingerprint encoding, the ordering of the condition write against the queue mutation, and the persisted `status.draAccounting` marker all belong to `KueueDRAIntegration`, and every one of them reaches an `Exactly` request with this gate off. Approving a child Alpha gate should not also approve an outcome protocol for the integration that is already Beta.

What the KEP carries now is the property each of them existed to provide, written as a requirement the parent path has to meet: a rejection that can be cleared, a charge that stops being actionable once the revision it was computed from moves, a commit that refuses rather than overwrites, one resource view shared by the DRA pass and the build, and a pass that refuses the whole request when it cannot value one alternative. The mechanism is kept for whoever implements it rather than deleted.

What drew the line was counting the identifiers in this branch's base. `DRAAccountingBlocked`, `WorkloadDRAReason` and `status.draAccounting` appear nowhere in `main`'s copy of the KEP, so this PR introduced them; `PreprocessedDRA` and the existing `Requeued`/`Inadmissible` latch do appear there, so references to those stayed.

Grepping for those names was not enough on its own. Four test entries turned on the condition write, one on the reservation marker, seven Alpha criteria required its field manager and its latch, and a block of the queue section designed the two write orderings and the ways a condition patch can fail, none of them naming a type this PR introduced. Those went too.

Two smaller things in the same pass. The prerequisite section keeps its nineteen invariant rows; the dependency graph after it named the state of eight open pull requests and went stale inside a week, so it moves to the implementation PR. And two assertions no longer pin the admissible range to the `Unlimited` sentinel, since #15026 is removing it.

On the Alpha boundary I asked about last round: the KEP now records the decision rather than the question. The upper-bound guarantee is scoped to an unchanged `ResourceClaimTemplate` identity and quota-affecting spec from the reservation through claim creation, and the generic binding is a pre-Beta re-evaluation on the child gate. #13842 is inherited from the existing `Exactly` path rather than introduced here.

@mimowo @tenzen-y, if that assumption is not acceptable for Alpha, I will move #13842 into the prerequisite set instead. I have deliberately not proposed the obvious-looking fixes: a second read before reserving or before unsuspending leaves the same window open between the read and claim creation, and rewriting `status.admission` when a template moves would cut against the point-in-time snapshot model.

@kannon92 @sohankunkerkar, the capacity thread is the one open question from the DRA side: under a source-less mapping the declared count stays the count-quota charge whether `capacity` is explicit or defaulted, and a mapping with a counter or capacity source keeps the whole request rejected.

Disclosure: I used an AI assistant while preparing this change.

### Comment by [@sohankunkerkar](https://github.com/sohankunkerkar) — 2026-09-21T18:51:04Z

@tenzen-y you raised concurrent admission in one of the review comments , so I traced it in code. Summary for you and @thc1006.

It does not affect the envelope. `generateVariant` makes one variant per flavor, not per alternative, and the webhook caps that at 16 with one resource group, so eight alternatives multiply into nothing. `IsFlavorAllowedForVariant` keeps each variant on its own flavor, so no two charge the same pool. `GetOrCompile` keys the cache on the expression text, so the CEL cost does not multiply either. I found no path where the envelope escapes its bound.

It actually mitigates the one real gap. `whenCanBorrow` defaults to `MayStopSearch`, so the assigner stops at the first flavor that fits and charges the whole envelope there. For the KEP's story, one H100 or else two A100s on one logical resource with a flavor per model: the envelope is 2, it lands entirely on whichever flavor is declared first, and the pods get that flavor's node labels. The other alternative then has no devices to match, so the workload runs the cheap one holding the expensive charge, and the other flavor's quota is never touched. With concurrent admission each flavor is its own variant, so the fallback gets a chance.

That is what I think the KEP should address. It mentions flavors once, and the Alpha rule that all alternatives resolve to one logical resource makes multi-flavor coverage normal rather than a corner. Nothing is unsafe, the charge is never below what runs, but it can be priced against the wrong flavor. A documented limitation plus a Beta item for per-flavor envelopes, not an Alpha change.

Two things are not this feature's problem. The parent workload is DRA preprocessed every reconcile and the result dropped, since `handleDRA` has no parent guard and `AddOrUpdateWorkload` returns early for parents. And one misconfiguration yields a rejection on the parent plus one per variant, none clearing while #13969 is open. Both happen with a plain Exactly claim today, so I will file them separately.

### Comment by [@sohankunkerkar](https://github.com/sohankunkerkar) — 2026-09-25T03:35:20Z

@tenzen-y @mimowo I went over this design again and I realize there are a few gaps that @tenzen-y already called out in the review comments. I think the main issue is that upstream hasn't settled how quota and firstAvailable fit together. [KEP-4816](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/4816-dra-prioritized-list/README.md#resource-quota) says it "will not serve as a quota management feature",  kubernetes/kubernetes#141510  is still open on exactly this, and kubernetes/kubernetes#142339 would let a policy take part in the allocator's choice and if that lands, our design changes.

So I'd land only what we can charge exactly: alternatives with the same count on the same logical resource. No over-accounting, and it closes the gap where Kueue rejects every firstAvailable claim while upstream has it locked on. The envelope can wait until upstream settles. @thc1006 I know that cuts a lot of the work here.

This is how the narrowed scope works, with an example.

**Rule:** accept `firstAvailable` only when every alternative asks for the same count on classes mapped to the same logical resource, and charge that count once. After preprocessing the Workload looks exactly like an `Exactly` claim.

**Example.** Each of 4 Pods needs one A100 and doesn't care how it's exposed. On normal nodes an A100 shows up as a full GPU; on nodes in MIG mode the same card shows up as one whole-card MIG slice (`7g.80gb`). The claim asks for "a full A100, else the whole-card MIG slice", and both classes map to `nvidia.com/gpu`.

Both options are 1 GPU, so Kueue charges 1 per Pod, 4 in total. Whichever option kube-scheduler picks, each Pod uses 1, so the charge always matches what runs.

Pods of one Job can land on different options, since kube-scheduler picks per Pod. That can't change the total, because every option is 1 GPU.

**Rejected:** "1 H100, else 2 A100". One option uses 1 GPU and the other 2, so there's no correct charge at admission.

**Why this avoids over-accounting.** The charge always equals what runs, so everything that reads it sees real usage:
- **Preemption** evicts only as much as the Job will actually use.
- **Fair Sharing and AFS** see each tenant's real usage, so they stay accurate.
- **Quota and borrowing** hold exactly what's in use, with nothing stranded.
- **TAS** is unaffected. It never reads DRA charges, same as `Exactly` today.
- **ConcurrentAdmission** works as today: one variant per flavor, never per alternative, and each variant is charged the same count.
- **Turning the gate off** doesn't evict running Workloads. They keep their admitted charge.

```diff
@@ -1719,6 +1750,133 @@ Processing Flow:
 
 This architecture separates concerns between DRA processing (controller) and queue management (scheduler), enabling robust error handling and retry logic for DRA-specific operations.
 
+### Prioritized List Quota
+
+This section is gated behind the `KueueDRAIntegrationPrioritizedList` Kueue feature gate (Alpha,
+default off). It adds quota accounting for prioritized-list requests, expressed with the
+`firstAvailable` field of a `DeviceRequest` (the Kubernetes `DRAPrioritizedList` feature, GA in
+1.36). A `firstAvailable` request lists ordered alternatives; kube-scheduler selects exactly one at
+allocation time, which is not known when Kueue reserves quota. With the gate off, such requests
+remain rejected as before.
+
+#### Accounting rule
+
+For a top-level `firstAvailable` request `q` with alternatives `A_q`, Kueue resolves each
+subrequest's DeviceClass to its logical quota resource through `deviceClassMappings` and forms a
+non-negative charge vector `charge(q, a)` per alternative `a`. The request is charged the
+component-wise maximum:
+
+```text
+envelope(q)[r] = max over a in A_q of charge(q, a)[r]
+```
+
+The per-Pod DRA charge is the existing `Exactly` charges plus the sum, over all `firstAvailable`
+requests, of `envelope(q)`. PodSet scaling is unchanged: the per-Pod charge is multiplied by the
+effective PodSet count by the existing workload-request calculation.
+
+Device-count sums use saturating `int64` arithmetic (`utilmath.SaturatingAdd`, as in
+`countDevicesPerClass`), so no envelope or per-request sum wraps negative. Charges that map to the
+same logical resource are then combined as `resource.Quantity` before being converted back to
+`int64`. That conversion must clamp an out-of-range quantity rather than call `Value()` directly,
+using the `SafeValue` helper added for the counter and capacity paths; the prioritized-list path
+must not introduce a new unclamped conversion. This overflow window is a pre-existing property of
+the shared count path (several DeviceClasses mapping to one logical resource near `MaxInt64`); the
+component-wise maximum keeps the envelope itself bounded, and tests cover multiple `firstAvailable`
+requests, `Exactly` plus `firstAvailable` on one resource, and PodSet scaling near `MaxInt64`.
+
+The maximum is taken after DeviceClass-to-logical-resource mapping. Two DeviceClasses may
+intentionally map to one logical resource (for example an H100 and an A100 class both mapping to a
+`gpu` resource); taking the maximum per DeviceClass and then summing the mapped classes would
+overcharge in that case.
+
+#### Safety argument
+
+kube-scheduler selects exactly one subrequest from each `firstAvailable`, so for every logical
+resource `r` the selected alternative's charge is at most `envelope(q)[r]`. Summing over all
+top-level requests, the realized charge cannot exceed the admitted envelope. This holds only if
+every alternative resolves to a complete, non-negative charge vector; unmapped, unsupported, or
+unknown forms are rejected rather than charged.
+
+#### Scope
+
+Supported: `ResourceClaimTemplate` references; `ExactCount` subrequests; count-based
+`deviceClassMappings` (no `sources`); request-selector CEL compilation.
+
+Rejected: direct `ResourceClaim` references; `All` and unknown allocation modes; unmapped
+DeviceClasses; and any alternative whose DeviceClass mapping configures a counter or capacity
+`source`. Source-backed alternatives are excluded because the counter and consumable-capacity
+accounting paths process only `Exactly` requests today; they can be added later by charging each
+alternative through its source path and taking the component-wise maximum of the resulting vectors.
+
+CEL selectors in every subrequest are compiled and syntax-checked. The `Exactly`
+device-cardinality check against ResourceSlices is not reused, because it would require every
+alternative to be satisfiable while only one has to be; the initial scope compiles CEL but skips
+that cardinality check for `firstAvailable`. Skipping it does not affect quota safety, since the
+envelope depends only on the declared counts; it can, however, let an unschedulable workload hold
+the envelope reservation. `WaitForPodsReady`, when enabled, eventually releases that reservation.
+It is a liveness and utilization safety net, not a premise of the quota upper bound; admission-time
+feasibility may reduce such cases in the future.
```

### Review by [@thc1006](https://github.com/thc1006) (commented) — 2026-08-01T12:34:09Z

- **keps/2941-DRA/README.md:1818** by [@thc1006](https://github.com/thc1006) — 2026-08-01T12:34:09Z
```diff
@@ -1719,6 +1750,133 @@ Processing Flow:
 
 This architecture separates concerns between DRA processing (controller) and queue management (scheduler), enabling robust error handling and retry logic for DRA-specific operations.
 
+### Prioritized List Quota
+
+This section is gated behind the `KueueDRAIntegrationPrioritizedList` Kueue feature gate (Alpha,
+default off). It adds quota accounting for prioritized-list requests, expressed with the
+`firstAvailable` field of a `DeviceRequest` (the Kubernetes `DRAPrioritizedList` feature, GA in
+1.36). A `firstAvailable` request lists ordered alternatives; kube-scheduler selects exactly one at
+allocation time, which is not known when Kueue reserves quota. With the gate off, such requests
+remain rejected as before.
+
+#### Accounting rule
+
+For a top-level `firstAvailable` request `q` with alternatives `A_q`, Kueue resolves each
+subrequest's DeviceClass to its logical quota resource through `deviceClassMappings` and forms a
+non-negative charge vector `charge(q, a)` per alternative `a`. The request is charged the
+component-wise maximum:
+
+```text
+envelope(q)[r] = max over a in A_q of charge(q, a)[r]
+```
+
+The per-Pod DRA charge is the existing `Exactly` charges plus the sum, over all `firstAvailable`
+requests, of `envelope(q)`. PodSet scaling is unchanged: the per-Pod charge is multiplied by the
+effective PodSet count by the existing workload-request calculation.
+
+Device-count sums use saturating `int64` arithmetic (`utilmath.SaturatingAdd`, as in
+`countDevicesPerClass`), so no envelope or per-request sum wraps negative. Charges that map to the
+same logical resource are then combined as `resource.Quantity` before being converted back to
+`int64`. That conversion must clamp an out-of-range quantity rather than call `Value()` directly,
+using the `SafeValue` helper added for the counter and capacity paths; the prioritized-list path
+must not introduce a new unclamped conversion. This overflow window is a pre-existing property of
+the shared count path (several DeviceClasses mapping to one logical resource near `MaxInt64`); the
+component-wise maximum keeps the envelope itself bounded, and tests cover multiple `firstAvailable`
+requests, `Exactly` plus `firstAvailable` on one resource, and PodSet scaling near `MaxInt64`.
+
+The maximum is taken after DeviceClass-to-logical-resource mapping. Two DeviceClasses may
+intentionally map to one logical resource (for example an H100 and an A100 class both mapping to a
+`gpu` resource); taking the maximum per DeviceClass and then summing the mapped classes would
+overcharge in that case.
+
+#### Safety argument
+
+kube-scheduler selects exactly one subrequest from each `firstAvailable`, so for every logical
+resource `r` the selected alternative's charge is at most `envelope(q)[r]`. Summing over all
+top-level requests, the realized charge cannot exceed the admitted envelope. This holds only if
+every alternative resolves to a complete, non-negative charge vector; unmapped, unsupported, or
+unknown forms are rejected rather than charged.
+
+#### Scope
+
+Supported: `ResourceClaimTemplate` references; `ExactCount` subrequests; count-based
+`deviceClassMappings` (no `sources`); request-selector CEL compilation.
+
+Rejected: direct `ResourceClaim` references; `All` and unknown allocation modes; unmapped
+DeviceClasses; and any alternative whose DeviceClass mapping configures a counter or capacity
+`source`. Source-backed alternatives are excluded because the counter and consumable-capacity
+accounting paths process only `Exactly` requests today; they can be added later by charging each
+alternative through its source path and taking the component-wise maximum of the resulting vectors.
+
+CEL selectors in every subrequest are compiled and syntax-checked. The `Exactly`
+device-cardinality check against ResourceSlices is not reused, because it would require every
+alternative to be satisfiable while only one has to be; the initial scope compiles CEL but skips
+that cardinality check for `firstAvailable`. Skipping it does not affect quota safety, since the
+envelope depends only on the declared counts; it can, however, let an unschedulable workload hold
+the envelope reservation. `WaitForPodsReady`, when enabled, eventually releases that reservation.
+It is a liveness and utilization safety net, not a premise of the quota upper bound; admission-time
+feasibility may reduce such cases in the future.
```

  You are right, and it contradicts the CEL paragraph in this same document. That paragraph says Kueue has no ResourceSlice informer and that inadmissible workloads only come back on ClusterQueue events, so my sentence claimed a mechanism the KEP explicitly says is not there.
  
  Rewritten to say what happens today: re-evaluation waits for a ClusterQueue event, which is the same recovery path and the same limitation the CEL check already carries in both directions, and `WaitForPodsReady` releases a reservation that never becomes schedulable. Event-driven requeuing on ResourceSlice changes is already an Alpha graduation criterion here, so it covers this path rather than needing a second one.

+#### Coordination with feasibility
+
+This quota accounting is independently safe: the envelope is a conservative upper bound and does
+not depend on any feasibility check. Two related efforts inform admission accuracy and are linked
+here but do not block this KEP: the TAS+DRA work
+([#10548](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/10548)), and the broader admission-time
+scheduling-feasibility umbrella
+([#12422](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/12422)), which passes the full claim spec
+to `structured.Allocator`.
+
+Two properties must be distinguished:
+
+- Static support: whether Kueue can correctly account for a request shape. Unsupported shapes (for
+  example a source-backed alternative in the initial scope) are permanent errors, rejected as
+  inadmissible.

+  supported-but-infeasible claim is retryable rather than a permanent error. Kueue has no
+  ResourceSlice informer today, so it is re-evaluated on ClusterQueue events, the same recovery

+a shared helper, so a claim is never accepted by one and rejected by the other. A feasibility
+result of "infeasible" must not be surfaced as "unsupported".

```

  Core `ResourceQuota` (KEP-4816) charges the worst-case device count per DeviceClass i.e. the maximum across all subrequests referencing that class. Kueue's envelope applies the same per-class maximum but adds a mapping layer: when an administrator maps several DeviceClasses to one Kueue logical resource, the envelope collapses to the per-resource maximum rather than maintaining separate per-class maxima. Namespace `ResourceQuota` and Kueue ClusterQueue quota may both apply to the same workload; this design does not let a user use firstAvailable to bypass namespace ResourceQuota.

```diff
@@ -1719,6 +1750,138 @@ Processing Flow:
 
 This architecture separates concerns between DRA processing (controller) and queue management (scheduler), enabling robust error handling and retry logic for DRA-specific operations.
 
+### Prioritized List Quota
+
+This section is gated behind the `KueueDRAIntegrationPrioritizedList` Kueue feature gate (Alpha,
+default off). It adds quota accounting for prioritized-list requests, expressed with the
+`firstAvailable` field of a `DeviceRequest` (the Kubernetes `DRAPrioritizedList` feature, GA in
+1.36). A `firstAvailable` request lists ordered alternatives; kube-scheduler selects exactly one at
+allocation time, which is not known when Kueue reserves quota. With the gate off, such requests
+remain rejected as before.
+
+#### Accounting rule
+
+For a top-level `firstAvailable` request `q` with alternatives `A_q`, Kueue resolves each
+subrequest's DeviceClass to its logical quota resource through `deviceClassMappings` and forms a
+non-negative charge vector `charge(q, a)` per alternative `a`. The request is charged the
+component-wise maximum:
+
+```text
+envelope(q)[r] = max over a in A_q of charge(q, a)[r]
+```
+
+The per-Pod DRA charge is the existing `Exactly` charges plus the sum, over all `firstAvailable`
+requests, of `envelope(q)`. PodSet scaling is unchanged: the per-Pod charge is multiplied by the
+effective PodSet count by the existing workload-request calculation.
+
+Device-count sums use saturating `int64` arithmetic (`utilmath.SaturatingAdd`, as in
+`countDevicesPerClass`), so no envelope or per-request sum wraps negative. Charges that map to the
+same logical resource are then combined as `resource.Quantity` before being converted back to
+`int64`. That conversion must clamp an out-of-range quantity rather than call `Value()` directly,
+using the `SafeValue` helper added for the counter and capacity paths; the prioritized-list path
+must not introduce a new unclamped conversion. This overflow window is a pre-existing property of
+the shared count path (several DeviceClasses mapping to one logical resource near `MaxInt64`); the
+component-wise maximum keeps the envelope itself bounded, and tests cover multiple `firstAvailable`
+requests, `Exactly` plus `firstAvailable` on one resource, and PodSet scaling near `MaxInt64`.
+
+The maximum is taken after DeviceClass-to-logical-resource mapping. Two DeviceClasses may
+intentionally map to one logical resource (for example an H100 and an A100 class both mapping to a
+`gpu` resource); taking the maximum per DeviceClass and then summing the mapped classes would
+overcharge in that case.
+
+#### Safety argument
+
+kube-scheduler selects exactly one subrequest from each `firstAvailable`, so for every logical
+resource `r` the selected alternative's charge is at most `envelope(q)[r]`. Summing over all
+top-level requests, the realized charge cannot exceed the admitted envelope. This holds only if
+every alternative resolves to a complete, non-negative charge vector; unmapped, unsupported, or
+unknown forms are rejected rather than charged.
+
+#### Scope
+
+Supported: `ResourceClaimTemplate` references; `ExactCount` subrequests; count-based
+`deviceClassMappings` (no `sources`); request-selector CEL compilation.
+
+Rejected: direct `ResourceClaim` references; `All` and unknown allocation modes; unmapped
```

 This architecture separates concerns between DRA processing (controller) and queue management (scheduler), enabling robust error handling and retry logic for DRA-specific operations.
 
+### Prioritized List Quota
+
+This section is gated behind the `KueueDRAIntegrationPrioritizedList` Kueue feature gate (Alpha,
+default off). It adds quota accounting for prioritized-list requests, expressed with the
+`firstAvailable` field of a `DeviceRequest` (the Kubernetes `DRAPrioritizedList` feature, GA in
+1.36). A `firstAvailable` request lists ordered alternatives; kube-scheduler selects exactly one at
+allocation time, which is not known when Kueue reserves quota. With the gate off, such requests
+remain rejected as before.
+
+#### Accounting rule
+
+For a top-level `firstAvailable` request `q` with alternatives `A_q`, Kueue resolves each
+subrequest's DeviceClass to its logical quota resource through `deviceClassMappings` and forms a
+non-negative charge vector `charge(q, a)` per alternative `a`. The request is charged the
+component-wise maximum:
+
+```text
+envelope(q)[r] = max over a in A_q of charge(q, a)[r]
+```
+
+The per-Pod DRA charge is the existing `Exactly` charges plus the sum, over all `firstAvailable`
+requests, of `envelope(q)`. PodSet scaling is unchanged: the per-Pod charge is multiplied by the
+effective PodSet count by the existing workload-request calculation.
+
+Device-count sums use saturating `int64` arithmetic (`utilmath.SaturatingAdd`, as in
+`countDevicesPerClass`), so no envelope or per-request sum wraps negative. Charges that map to the
+same logical resource are then combined as `resource.Quantity` before being converted back to
+`int64`. That conversion must clamp an out-of-range quantity rather than call `Value()` directly,
+using the `SafeValue` helper added for the counter and capacity paths; the prioritized-list path
+must not introduce a new unclamped conversion. This overflow window is a pre-existing property of
+the shared count path (several DeviceClasses mapping to one logical resource near `MaxInt64`); the
+component-wise maximum keeps the envelope itself bounded, and tests cover multiple `firstAvailable`
+requests, `Exactly` plus `firstAvailable` on one resource, and PodSet scaling near `MaxInt64`.
+
+The maximum is taken after DeviceClass-to-logical-resource mapping. Two DeviceClasses may
+intentionally map to one logical resource (for example an H100 and an A100 class both mapping to a
+`gpu` resource); taking the maximum per DeviceClass and then summing the mapped classes would
+overcharge in that case.
+
+#### Safety argument
+
+kube-scheduler selects exactly one subrequest from each `firstAvailable`, so for every logical
+resource `r` the selected alternative's charge is at most `envelope(q)[r]`. Summing over all
+top-level requests, the realized charge cannot exceed the admitted envelope. This holds only if
+every alternative resolves to a complete, non-negative charge vector; unmapped, unsupported, or
+unknown forms are rejected rather than charged.
+
+#### Scope
+
+Supported: `ResourceClaimTemplate` references; `ExactCount` subrequests; count-based
+`deviceClassMappings` (no `sources`); request-selector CEL compilation.
+
+Rejected: direct `ResourceClaim` references; `All` and unknown allocation modes; unmapped
+DeviceClasses; and any alternative whose DeviceClass mapping configures a counter or capacity
+`source`. Source-backed alternatives are excluded because the counter and consumable-capacity
+accounting paths process only `Exactly` requests today; they can be added later by charging each
+alternative through its source path and taking the component-wise maximum of the resulting vectors.
+
```

  Note: the existing Exactly path skips counter/capacity DeviceClasses at the count level (deferring to the counter/capacity pipelines). For firstAvailable, skipping would break the envelope precondition; the implementation must reject the entire request if any alternative's DeviceClass has source configs.

+Two properties must be distinguished:

+- Static support: whether Kueue can correctly account for a request shape. Unsupported shapes (for
+  example a source-backed alternative in the initial scope) are permanent errors, rejected as

+a shared helper, so a claim is never accepted by one and rejected by the other. A feasibility
+result of "infeasible" must not be surfaced as "unsupported".

The mapping-layer difference and your no-bypass point are both in the section now.

  Fair, the phrase was doing no work as written. The Beta criterion now names the three places a charge is aggregated: the per-Pod sum across requests, the PodSet-count multiplication, and the `resource.Quantity` to `int64` conversion where several DeviceClasses map to one logical resource. The maximum over alternatives is deliberately not in that list, since it cannot produce a value larger than one it already held.

```diff
@@ -1719,6 +1750,138 @@ Processing Flow:
 
 This architecture separates concerns between DRA processing (controller) and queue management (scheduler), enabling robust error handling and retry logic for DRA-specific operations.
 
+### Prioritized List Quota
+
+This section is gated behind the `KueueDRAIntegrationPrioritizedList` Kueue feature gate (Alpha,
+default off). It adds quota accounting for prioritized-list requests, expressed with the
+`firstAvailable` field of a `DeviceRequest` (the Kubernetes `DRAPrioritizedList` feature, GA in
+1.36). A `firstAvailable` request lists ordered alternatives; kube-scheduler selects exactly one at
+allocation time, which is not known when Kueue reserves quota. With the gate off, such requests
+remain rejected as before.
+
+#### Accounting rule
+
+For a top-level `firstAvailable` request `q` with alternatives `A_q`, Kueue resolves each
+subrequest's DeviceClass to its logical quota resource through `deviceClassMappings` and forms a
+non-negative charge vector `charge(q, a)` per alternative `a`. The request is charged the
+component-wise maximum:
+
+```text
+envelope(q)[r] = max over a in A_q of charge(q, a)[r]
+```
+
+The per-Pod DRA charge is the existing `Exactly` charges plus the sum, over all `firstAvailable`
+requests, of `envelope(q)`. PodSet scaling is unchanged: the per-Pod charge is multiplied by the
+effective PodSet count by the existing workload-request calculation.
+
+Device-count sums use saturating `int64` arithmetic (`utilmath.SaturatingAdd`, as in
+`countDevicesPerClass`), so no envelope or per-request sum wraps negative. Charges that map to the
+same logical resource are then combined as `resource.Quantity` before being converted back to
+`int64`. That conversion must clamp an out-of-range quantity rather than call `Value()` directly,
+using the `SafeValue` helper added for the counter and capacity paths; the prioritized-list path
+must not introduce a new unclamped conversion. This overflow window is a pre-existing property of
+the shared count path (several DeviceClasses mapping to one logical resource near `MaxInt64`); the
+component-wise maximum keeps the envelope itself bounded, and tests cover multiple `firstAvailable`
+requests, `Exactly` plus `firstAvailable` on one resource, and PodSet scaling near `MaxInt64`.
+
+The maximum is taken after DeviceClass-to-logical-resource mapping. Two DeviceClasses may
+intentionally map to one logical resource (for example an H100 and an A100 class both mapping to a
+`gpu` resource); taking the maximum per DeviceClass and then summing the mapped classes would
+overcharge in that case.
+
+#### Safety argument
+
+kube-scheduler selects exactly one subrequest from each `firstAvailable`, so for every logical
+resource `r` the selected alternative's charge is at most `envelope(q)[r]`. Summing over all
+top-level requests, the realized charge cannot exceed the admitted envelope. This holds only if
+every alternative resolves to a complete, non-negative charge vector; unmapped, unsupported, or
+unknown forms are rejected rather than charged.
+
+#### Scope
+
+Supported: `ResourceClaimTemplate` references; `ExactCount` subrequests; count-based
+`deviceClassMappings` (no `sources`); request-selector CEL compilation.
+
+Rejected: direct `ResourceClaim` references; `All` and unknown allocation modes; unmapped
```

 This architecture separates concerns between DRA processing (controller) and queue management (scheduler), enabling robust error handling and retry logic for DRA-specific operations.

+
+This section is gated behind the `KueueDRAIntegrationPrioritizedList` Kueue feature gate (Alpha,

+For a top-level `firstAvailable` request `q` with alternatives `A_q`, Kueue resolves each

+```
+

+requests, of `envelope(q)`. PodSet scaling is unchanged: the per-Pod charge is multiplied by the

+`countDevicesPerClass`), so no envelope or per-request sum wraps negative. Charges that map to the
+same logical resource are then combined as `resource.Quantity` before being converted back to
+`int64`. That conversion must clamp an out-of-range quantity rather than call `Value()` directly,
+using the `SafeValue` helper added for the counter and capacity paths; the prioritized-list path
+must not introduce a new unclamped conversion. This overflow window is a pre-existing property of
+the shared count path (several DeviceClasses mapping to one logical resource near `MaxInt64`); the
+component-wise maximum keeps the envelope itself bounded, and tests cover multiple `firstAvailable`
+requests, `Exactly` plus `firstAvailable` on one resource, and PodSet scaling near `MaxInt64`.

+intentionally map to one logical resource (for example an H100 and an A100 class both mapping to a
+`gpu` resource); taking the maximum per DeviceClass and then summing the mapped classes would
+overcharge in that case.

+
+kube-scheduler selects exactly one subrequest from each `firstAvailable`, so for every logical
+resource `r` the selected alternative's charge is at most `envelope(q)[r]`. Summing over all
+top-level requests, the realized charge cannot exceed the admitted envelope. This holds only if
+every alternative resolves to a complete, non-negative charge vector; unmapped, unsupported, or
+unknown forms are rejected rather than charged.

+

### Review by [@sohankunkerkar](https://github.com/sohankunkerkar) (commented) — 2026-08-06T22:08:54Z

- **keps/2941-DRA/README.md:1860** by [@sohankunkerkar](https://github.com/sohankunkerkar) — 2026-08-06T21:27:10Z
```diff
@@ -1719,6 +1755,247 @@ Processing Flow:
 
 This architecture separates concerns between DRA processing (controller) and queue management (scheduler), enabling robust error handling and retry logic for DRA-specific operations.
 
+### Prioritized List Quota
+
+This section is gated behind the `KueueDRAIntegrationPrioritizedList` Kueue feature gate (Alpha,
+default off). It adds quota accounting for prioritized-list requests, expressed with the
+`firstAvailable` field of a `DeviceRequest` (the Kubernetes `DRAPrioritizedList` feature, GA in
+1.36). A `firstAvailable` request lists ordered alternatives, at most eight of them
+(`FirstAvailableDeviceRequestMaxSize`); kube-scheduler selects exactly one at allocation time, which
+is not known when Kueue reserves quota. With the gate off, such requests remain rejected as
+before.
+
+#### Accounting rule
+
+For a top-level `firstAvailable` request `q` with alternatives `A_q`, Kueue resolves each
+subrequest's DeviceClass to its logical quota resource through `deviceClassMappings` and forms a
+non-negative charge vector `charge(q, a)` per alternative `a`. `DeviceSubRequest` has no
+`adminAccess` field, so admin access cannot appear on an alternative and its zero-charge rule stays
+confined to `Exactly` requests. The request is charged the component-wise maximum:
+
+```text
+envelope(q)[r] = max over a in A_q of charge(q, a)[r]
+```
+
+The per-Pod DRA charge is the existing `Exactly` charges plus the sum, over all `firstAvailable`
+requests, of `envelope(q)`. PodSet scaling is unchanged: the per-Pod charge is multiplied by the
+effective PodSet count by the existing workload-request calculation. With
+`ElasticJobsViaWorkloadSlices`, each slice carries its own PodSet count, so each computes its
+envelope independently and multiplies the same per-Pod envelope by its own count; nothing is shared
+between the slices of one Job.
+
+Saturating arithmetic stops a sum from wrapping, but a saturated sum no longer stands for the value
+it replaced, so it cannot carry the bound: clamping to `MaxInt64` reports less than the total it
+came from. The merge into `resources.Requests` is weaker still, since `MapRequests.Add` uses plain
+`+` and can wrap negative where a DRA logical resource shares a key with an ordinary Pod resource. A
+charge that cannot be represented exactly as `int64` therefore makes the workload inadmissible
+rather than being clamped and admitted, at each step that can produce one: the per-Pod sum across
+requests, the merge with ordinary resources, and the PodSet-count multiplication. Nor is a saturated
+aggregate divided to recover a smaller request: `PodSetResources` scaling divides by the old count
+and multiplies by the new, so partial admission, `ReclaimablePods`, and workload-slice replacement
+recompute from the per-Pod envelope instead.
+
+Converting a combined `resource.Quantity` back to `int64` follows the unit convention in
+`resources.ResourceValue`, milli-units for `cpu` and absolute units otherwise. That helper calls
+`Value()` for everything but `cpu`, so following it is not on its own enough: a quantity that does
+not fit has to be reported rather than silently truncated, which is what makes the rejection above
+possible. Nothing currently stops an administrator from naming a logical resource `cpu`, where an
+unconditional `SafeValue` would read `8` as 8 milliCPU. The component-wise maximum keeps the
+envelope itself bounded, and tests cover multiple `firstAvailable` requests, `Exactly` plus
+`firstAvailable` on one resource, and PodSet scaling past the representable range.
+
+The same check is needed wherever these quantities are summed, not only within a Pod. Two PodSets
+can each have a representable total for a logical resource while the sum across PodSets does not
+fit in an `int64`.
+
+There is currently no way to report any of this. `totalRequestsFromPodSets` returns
+`[]PodSetResources` and no error, and `NewInfo` and `Info.Update` do not return errors either. The
+implementation will need to add an error path, so that the workload can be marked inadmissible
+instead of saturating. Until that exists, the Alpha bound holds for charges the shared path can
+represent, which is the condition the existing `Exactly` charges already depend on.
+
+The maximum is taken after DeviceClass-to-logical-resource mapping. Two DeviceClasses may
+intentionally map to one logical resource (for example an H100 and an A100 class both mapping to a
+`gpu` resource); taking the maximum per DeviceClass and then summing the mapped classes would
+overcharge in that case.
+
+The envelope is a bound in resource space, and it does not record which ResourceFlavor an
+alternative would have used. When two alternatives map to different logical resources, Kueue
+assigns a flavor to each one, and `podset.FromAssignment` copies the node labels of every assigned
+flavor into the same PodSet. `podSetAssignments[].flavors` is a map, so when two of those flavors
+set the same label key, the value that survives depends on map iteration order. This is not
+specific to prioritized lists, since any PodSet assigned two such flavors behaves the same way, but
+a prioritized list makes it easy to reach: the alternatives are mutually exclusive, and a user is
+likely to expect a fallback rather than the labels of both branches. For Alpha, the logical
+resources used by prioritized-list alternatives are expected to use flavors whose node labels do
+not conflict. DRA flavors normally carry none.
+
+#### Safety argument
+
+kube-scheduler selects exactly one subrequest from each `firstAvailable`, so for every logical
+resource `r` the selected alternative's charge is at most `envelope(q)[r]`. Summing over all
+top-level requests, the realized charge cannot exceed the admitted envelope. This holds only if
+every alternative resolves to a complete, non-negative charge vector; unmapped, unsupported, or
+unknown forms are rejected rather than charged. This only covers the request forms that exist in
+the Kubernetes API version Kueue is compiled against. A classifier written over the Go types cannot
+see a field that was added in a later Kubernetes minor release, so bumping the API dependency will
+require reviewing any new fields that affect the charge.
+
+The subrequest fields Kueue can see today, and how the classifier treats each one:
+
+| Field | Treatment |
+| --- | --- |
+| `deviceClassName` | maps to the logical resource; an unmapped class is rejected |
+| `allocationMode` | only an effective `ExactCount` is charged |
+| `count` | the charge itself |
+| `selectors` | compiled, and otherwise not part of the charge |
+| `tolerations` | feasibility only, and not part of the charge |
+
+The API specifies the defaults, so the classifier reads effective values: an omitted
+`allocationMode` is `ExactCount`, and an omitted `count` under that mode is one. The same type
+states that clients must refuse to handle requests with unknown modes, which is what the rejection
+above does. Claim-level `constraints` and `config` do not change the device count, and `pkg/dra`
+does not read them.
+
+Kubernetes 1.37 adds `capacity` and `derivedAttributes` to `DeviceSubRequest`. Kueue is compiled
```

  This [line](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/blob/main/vendor/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go#L1252) has `Capacity *CapacityRequirements` on DeviceSubRequest. Only derivedAttributes is 1.37-only, which means only `derivedAttributes` is invisible at 1.36, capacity can be classified now.

+envelope independently and multiplies the same per-Pod envelope by its own count; nothing is shared
+between the slices of one Job.
+
+Saturating arithmetic stops a sum from wrapping, but a saturated sum no longer stands for the value
+it replaced, so it cannot carry the bound: clamping to `MaxInt64` reports less than the total it
+came from. The merge into `resources.Requests` is weaker still, since `MapRequests.Add` uses plain
+`+` and can wrap negative where a DRA logical resource shares a key with an ordinary Pod resource. A
+charge that cannot be represented exactly as `int64` therefore makes the workload inadmissible
+rather than being clamped and admitted, at each step that can produce one: the per-Pod sum across
+requests, the merge with ordinary resources, and the PodSet-count multiplication. Nor is a saturated
+aggregate divided to recover a smaller request: `PodSetResources` scaling divides by the old count
+and multiplies by the new, so partial admission, `ReclaimablePods`, and workload-slice replacement
+recompute from the per-Pod envelope instead.
+
+Converting a combined `resource.Quantity` back to `int64` follows the unit convention in
+`resources.ResourceValue`, milli-units for `cpu` and absolute units otherwise. That helper calls
+`Value()` for everything but `cpu`, so following it is not on its own enough: a quantity that does
+not fit has to be reported rather than silently truncated, which is what makes the rejection above
+possible. Nothing currently stops an administrator from naming a logical resource `cpu`, where an
+unconditional `SafeValue` would read `8` as 8 milliCPU. The component-wise maximum keeps the
+envelope itself bounded, and tests cover multiple `firstAvailable` requests, `Exactly` plus
+`firstAvailable` on one resource, and PodSet scaling past the representable range.
+
+The same check is needed wherever these quantities are summed, not only within a Pod. Two PodSets
+can each have a representable total for a logical resource while the sum across PodSets does not
+fit in an `int64`.
+
+There is currently no way to report any of this. `totalRequestsFromPodSets` returns
+`[]PodSetResources` and no error, and `NewInfo` and `Info.Update` do not return errors either. The
+implementation will need to add an error path, so that the workload can be marked inadmissible
+instead of saturating. Until that exists, the Alpha bound holds for charges the shared path can
+represent, which is the condition the existing `Exactly` charges already depend on.
+
+The maximum is taken after DeviceClass-to-logical-resource mapping. Two DeviceClasses may
+intentionally map to one logical resource (for example an H100 and an A100 class both mapping to a
+`gpu` resource); taking the maximum per DeviceClass and then summing the mapped classes would
+overcharge in that case.
+
+The envelope is a bound in resource space, and it does not record which ResourceFlavor an
+alternative would have used. When two alternatives map to different logical resources, Kueue
+assigns a flavor to each one, and `podset.FromAssignment` copies the node labels of every assigned
+flavor into the same PodSet. `podSetAssignments[].flavors` is a map, so when two of those flavors
+set the same label key, the value that survives depends on map iteration order. This is not
+specific to prioritized lists, since any PodSet assigned two such flavors behaves the same way, but
+a prioritized list makes it easy to reach: the alternatives are mutually exclusive, and a user is
+likely to expect a fallback rather than the labels of both branches. For Alpha, the logical
+resources used by prioritized-list alternatives are expected to use flavors whose node labels do
+not conflict. DRA flavors normally carry none.
+
+#### Safety argument
+
+kube-scheduler selects exactly one subrequest from each `firstAvailable`, so for every logical

+top-level requests, the realized charge cannot exceed the admitted envelope. This holds only if

+unknown forms are rejected rather than charged. This only covers the request forms that exist in

+see a field that was added in a later Kubernetes minor release, so bumping the API dependency will
+require reviewing any new fields that affect the charge.
+

+| Field | Treatment |

@@ -1719,6 +1755,247 @@ Processing Flow:
 
 This architecture separates concerns between DRA processing (controller) and queue management (scheduler), enabling robust error handling and retry logic for DRA-specific operations.
 
+### Prioritized List Quota
+
+This section is gated behind the `KueueDRAIntegrationPrioritizedList` Kueue feature gate (Alpha,
+default off). It adds quota accounting for prioritized-list requests, expressed with the
+`firstAvailable` field of a `DeviceRequest` (the Kubernetes `DRAPrioritizedList` feature, GA in
+1.36). A `firstAvailable` request lists ordered alternatives, at most eight of them
+(`FirstAvailableDeviceRequestMaxSize`); kube-scheduler selects exactly one at allocation time, which
+is not known when Kueue reserves quota. With the gate off, such requests remain rejected as
+before.
+
+#### Accounting rule
+
+For a top-level `firstAvailable` request `q` with alternatives `A_q`, Kueue resolves each
+subrequest's DeviceClass to its logical quota resource through `deviceClassMappings` and forms a
+non-negative charge vector `charge(q, a)` per alternative `a`. `DeviceSubRequest` has no
+`adminAccess` field, so admin access cannot appear on an alternative and its zero-charge rule stays
+confined to `Exactly` requests. The request is charged the component-wise maximum:
+
+```text
+envelope(q)[r] = max over a in A_q of charge(q, a)[r]
+```
+
+The per-Pod DRA charge is the existing `Exactly` charges plus the sum, over all `firstAvailable`
+requests, of `envelope(q)`. PodSet scaling is unchanged: the per-Pod charge is multiplied by the
+effective PodSet count by the existing workload-request calculation. With
+`ElasticJobsViaWorkloadSlices`, each slice carries its own PodSet count, so each computes its
+envelope independently and multiplies the same per-Pod envelope by its own count; nothing is shared
+between the slices of one Job.
+
+Saturating arithmetic stops a sum from wrapping, but a saturated sum no longer stands for the value
+it replaced, so it cannot carry the bound: clamping to `MaxInt64` reports less than the total it
+came from. The merge into `resources.Requests` is weaker still, since `MapRequests.Add` uses plain
+`+` and can wrap negative where a DRA logical resource shares a key with an ordinary Pod resource. A
+charge that cannot be represented exactly as `int64` therefore makes the workload inadmissible
+rather than being clamped and admitted, at each step that can produce one: the per-Pod sum across
+requests, the merge with ordinary resources, and the PodSet-count multiplication. Nor is a saturated
+aggregate divided to recover a smaller request: `PodSetResources` scaling divides by the old count
+and multiplies by the new, so partial admission, `ReclaimablePods`, and workload-slice replacement
+recompute from the per-Pod envelope instead.
+
+Converting a combined `resource.Quantity` back to `int64` follows the unit convention in
+`resources.ResourceValue`, milli-units for `cpu` and absolute units otherwise. That helper calls
+`Value()` for everything but `cpu`, so following it is not on its own enough: a quantity that does
+not fit has to be reported rather than silently truncated, which is what makes the rejection above
+possible. Nothing currently stops an administrator from naming a logical resource `cpu`, where an
+unconditional `SafeValue` would read `8` as 8 milliCPU. The component-wise maximum keeps the
+envelope itself bounded, and tests cover multiple `firstAvailable` requests, `Exactly` plus
+`firstAvailable` on one resource, and PodSet scaling past the representable range.
+
+The same check is needed wherever these quantities are summed, not only within a Pod. Two PodSets
+can each have a representable total for a logical resource while the sum across PodSets does not
+fit in an `int64`.
+
+There is currently no way to report any of this. `totalRequestsFromPodSets` returns
+`[]PodSetResources` and no error, and `NewInfo` and `Info.Update` do not return errors either. The
+implementation will need to add an error path, so that the workload can be marked inadmissible
+instead of saturating. Until that exists, the Alpha bound holds for charges the shared path can
+represent, which is the condition the existing `Exactly` charges already depend on.
+
+The maximum is taken after DeviceClass-to-logical-resource mapping. Two DeviceClasses may
+intentionally map to one logical resource (for example an H100 and an A100 class both mapping to a
+`gpu` resource); taking the maximum per DeviceClass and then summing the mapped classes would
+overcharge in that case.
+
+The envelope is a bound in resource space, and it does not record which ResourceFlavor an
+alternative would have used. When two alternatives map to different logical resources, Kueue
+assigns a flavor to each one, and `podset.FromAssignment` copies the node labels of every assigned
+flavor into the same PodSet. `podSetAssignments[].flavors` is a map, so when two of those flavors
+set the same label key, the value that survives depends on map iteration order. This is not
+specific to prioritized lists, since any PodSet assigned two such flavors behaves the same way, but
+a prioritized list makes it easy to reach: the alternatives are mutually exclusive, and a user is
+likely to expect a fallback rather than the labels of both branches. For Alpha, the logical
+resources used by prioritized-list alternatives are expected to use flavors whose node labels do
+not conflict. DRA flavors normally carry none.
+
+#### Safety argument
+
+kube-scheduler selects exactly one subrequest from each `firstAvailable`, so for every logical
+resource `r` the selected alternative's charge is at most `envelope(q)[r]`. Summing over all
+top-level requests, the realized charge cannot exceed the admitted envelope. This holds only if
+every alternative resolves to a complete, non-negative charge vector; unmapped, unsupported, or
+unknown forms are rejected rather than charged. This only covers the request forms that exist in
+the Kubernetes API version Kueue is compiled against. A classifier written over the Go types cannot
+see a field that was added in a later Kubernetes minor release, so bumping the API dependency will
+require reviewing any new fields that affect the charge.
+
+The subrequest fields Kueue can see today, and how the classifier treats each one:
+
+| Field | Treatment |
+| --- | --- |
+| `deviceClassName` | maps to the logical resource; an unmapped class is rejected |
+| `allocationMode` | only an effective `ExactCount` is charged |
+| `count` | the charge itself |
+| `selectors` | compiled, and otherwise not part of the charge |
+| `tolerations` | feasibility only, and not part of the charge |
+
+The API specifies the defaults, so the classifier reads effective values: an omitted
+`allocationMode` is `ExactCount`, and an omitted `count` under that mode is one. The same type
+states that clients must refuse to handle requests with unknown modes, which is what the rejection
+above does. Claim-level `constraints` and `config` do not change the device count, and `pkg/dra`
+does not read them.
+
+Kubernetes 1.37 adds `capacity` and `derivedAttributes` to `DeviceSubRequest`. Kueue is compiled
+against 1.36, where the type ends at `tolerations`, so a 1.36 build talking to a 1.37 apiserver
+decodes a subrequest without either field and cannot reject an alternative that uses them. The
+envelope still charges the declared count, which is what a count-based mapping produces in any
+case, but deciding whether that is the right charge for a capacity request is what the
+capacity-backed rejection exists to do. Raising the dependency to 1.37 and classifying both fields
+is a prerequisite for this gate leaving Alpha.
+
+The bound rests on two further assumptions. First, the `ResourceClaimSpec` Kueue charges is the one
+later used to create the generated `ResourceClaim`. A `ResourceClaimTemplate` spec is immutable in
+place, but deleting and recreating one under the same name can change the spec between charging
+(while the workload is `Pending`) and claim generation, so the running claim could differ from the
+charged envelope. This gap is shared by all Kueue DRA charging, including the existing `Exactly`
+path, rather than introduced here. It is a known limitation tracked in
+[#13842](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/13842), and the bound above is stated for a
+fixed `ResourceClaimSpec` rather than made conditional on that issue landing first. Second, the
+bound covers the logical resources the target `ClusterQueue` manages; `quotaCheckStrategy:
+IgnoreUndeclared` deliberately omits undeclared dimensions from enforcement, so an alternative that
+resolves to an omitted resource is not charged.
+
+#### Scope
+
+Supported: `ResourceClaimTemplate` references; `ExactCount` subrequests; count-based
+`deviceClassMappings` (no `sources`); request-selector CEL compilation.
+
+Rejected: direct `ResourceClaim` references; `All` and unknown allocation modes; unmapped
+DeviceClasses; and any alternative whose DeviceClass mapping configures a counter or capacity
+`source`. Source-backed alternatives are excluded because the counter and consumable-capacity
+accounting paths process only `Exactly` requests today; they can be added later by charging each
+alternative through its source path and taking the component-wise maximum of the resulting vectors.
+
+CEL selectors in every subrequest are compiled and syntax-checked. The `Exactly`
+device-cardinality check against ResourceSlices is not reused, because it would require every
+alternative to be satisfiable while only one has to be; the initial scope compiles CEL but skips
+that cardinality check for `firstAvailable`. Skipping it does not affect quota safety, since the
+envelope depends only on the declared counts; it can, however, let an unschedulable workload hold
+the envelope reservation. `WaitForPodsReady`, when enabled, eventually releases that reservation.
+It is a liveness and utilization safety net, not a premise of the quota upper bound; admission-time
+feasibility may reduce such cases in the future.
+
+The compiler that check uses is shared with the `Exactly` path, and Kueue builds its cache with an
+empty `dracel.Features`. The apiserver compiles the same selectors with the consumable capacity and
+list attribute features available, so a selector it accepted can fail to compile in Kueue. That is
+not introduced here, but a classifier that compiles every alternative will hit it more often, so
+the two environments should be aligned before this scope is implemented.
+
+#### Coordination with feasibility
+
+This quota accounting is independently safe. Whichever alternative kube-scheduler picks, that
+alternative's charge is at most the envelope, so reserving the envelope cannot under-charge the
+allocation that follows. The argument never needs to predict the choice, so it does not rest on
+ResourceSlice inspection or on any node-level fit check. Two related efforts inform admission
+accuracy and are linked here but do not block this KEP: the TAS+DRA work
+([#10548](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/10548)), and the broader admission-time
+scheduling-feasibility umbrella
+([#12422](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/12422)), which passes the full claim spec
+to `structured.Allocator`.
+
+Two properties must be distinguished:
+
+- Static support: whether Kueue can correctly account for a request shape. Unsupported shapes are
+  permanent errors, rejected as inadmissible. Where one alternative carries a counter or capacity
+  source, the whole request is rejected rather than that alternative skipped: the envelope is a
+  maximum over every alternative, so dropping one of them stops bounding the allocation the
+  scheduler may still choose.
+- Dynamic feasibility: whether the current cluster state can schedule a supported claim. A
+  supported-but-infeasible claim is retryable rather than a permanent error. Kueue has a
+  ResourceSlice controller, but it builds its driver set from the `sources` of each device class
+  mapping and filters slice events on that set, so a count-only mapping registers no driver and its
+  slice changes trigger no requeue. The initial Alpha also reserves quota without running the
+  cardinality or allocator checks, so Kueue never produces a supported-but-infeasible result to
+  requeue in the first place; once quota is reserved, kube-scheduler owns dynamic feasibility and
+  retries the Pending Pod on ResourceClaim, DeviceClass, ResourceSlice, and node events. A workload
+  still waiting on quota is requeued on the next ClusterQueue event, and an admitted one whose Pod
+  never becomes schedulable holds its reservation until `WaitForPodsReady`, when enabled,
+  evicts it. Extending the controller to count-only mappings, or reaching feasibility through the
+  scheduler library, is a graduation criterion rather than something the current controller covers.
+
+The quota path MUST consume the static-support classification from a single helper, and any
+admission-time feasibility path MUST consume that same helper once one exists, so a claim is never
+accepted by one and rejected by the other. Splitting the two invites the failures that are hardest
+to notice: a shape the quota path charges and the feasibility path refuses forever, a shape the
+feasibility path admits and the quota path never charges, or a new API field that only one of them
+learns to reject. A feasibility result of "infeasible" must not be
+surfaced as "unsupported", and a failed object read or slice listing is neither.
+
+#### Relationship with Kubernetes ResourceQuota
+
+This is a Kueue-specific quota policy and does not change Kubernetes `ResourceQuota`. Core
+`ResourceQuota` (KEP-4816) takes, within each top-level `FirstAvailable`, the largest device count
```

+`+` and can wrap negative where a DRA logical resource shares a key with an ordinary Pod resource. A
+charge that cannot be represented exactly as `int64` therefore makes the workload inadmissible
+rather than being clamped and admitted, at each step that can produce one: the per-Pod sum across
+requests, the merge with ordinary resources, and the PodSet-count multiplication. Nor is a saturated
+aggregate divided to recover a smaller request: `PodSetResources` scaling divides by the old count
+and multiplies by the new, so partial admission, `ReclaimablePods`, and workload-slice replacement
+recompute from the per-Pod envelope instead.
+
+Converting a combined `resource.Quantity` back to `int64` follows the unit convention in
+`resources.ResourceValue`, milli-units for `cpu` and absolute units otherwise. That helper calls
+`Value()` for everything but `cpu`, so following it is not on its own enough: a quantity that does
+not fit has to be reported rather than silently truncated, which is what makes the rejection above
+possible. Nothing currently stops an administrator from naming a logical resource `cpu`, where an
+unconditional `SafeValue` would read `8` as 8 milliCPU. The component-wise maximum keeps the
+envelope itself bounded, and tests cover multiple `firstAvailable` requests, `Exactly` plus
+`firstAvailable` on one resource, and PodSet scaling past the representable range.
+
+The same check is needed wherever these quantities are summed, not only within a Pod. Two PodSets
+can each have a representable total for a logical resource while the sum across PodSets does not
+fit in an `int64`.
+
+There is currently no way to report any of this. `totalRequestsFromPodSets` returns
+`[]PodSetResources` and no error, and `NewInfo` and `Info.Update` do not return errors either. The
+implementation will need to add an error path, so that the workload can be marked inadmissible
+instead of saturating. Until that exists, the Alpha bound holds for charges the shared path can
+represent, which is the condition the existing `Exactly` charges already depend on.
+
+The maximum is taken after DeviceClass-to-logical-resource mapping. Two DeviceClasses may
+intentionally map to one logical resource (for example an H100 and an A100 class both mapping to a
+`gpu` resource); taking the maximum per DeviceClass and then summing the mapped classes would
+overcharge in that case.
+
+The envelope is a bound in resource space, and it does not record which ResourceFlavor an
+alternative would have used. When two alternatives map to different logical resources, Kueue
+assigns a flavor to each one, and `podset.FromAssignment` copies the node labels of every assigned
+flavor into the same PodSet. `podSetAssignments[].flavors` is a map, so when two of those flavors
+set the same label key, the value that survives depends on map iteration order. This is not
+specific to prioritized lists, since any PodSet assigned two such flavors behaves the same way, but
+a prioritized list makes it easy to reach: the alternatives are mutually exclusive, and a user is
+likely to expect a fallback rather than the labels of both branches. For Alpha, the logical
+resources used by prioritized-list alternatives are expected to use flavors whose node labels do
+not conflict. DRA flavors normally carry none.
+
+#### Safety argument
+
+kube-scheduler selects exactly one subrequest from each `firstAvailable`, so for every logical
+resource `r` the selected alternative's charge is at most `envelope(q)[r]`. Summing over all
+top-level requests, the realized charge cannot exceed the admitted envelope. This holds only if
+every alternative resolves to a complete, non-negative charge vector; unmapped, unsupported, or
+unknown forms are rejected rather than charged. This only covers the request forms that exist in
+the Kubernetes API version Kueue is compiled against. A classifier written over the Go types cannot
+see a field that was added in a later Kubernetes minor release, so bumping the API dependency will
+require reviewing any new fields that affect the charge.
+
+The subrequest fields Kueue can see today, and how the classifier treats each one:
+
+| Field | Treatment |
```

  Added, as rejected: the count path does not charge a consumable-capacity request, which is the same reason a capacity-backed mapping is refused. The rejected list in Scope says so too.
  
  That treatment follows from your note above about source configs breaking the envelope precondition rather than from anything the API forces, so it is a scope call. Say the word if you would rather it were charged at the declared count and left to the capacity path later.
